title: PRD: Partial-Egress Decomposition and Offline Upgrade Safety for Private/VPC Deploys
creator: Liam O'Connor
description:
Overview:
This PRD defines requirements and acceptance criteria for a partial-egress model and a hardened offline upgrade flow for Private/VPC deployments. The goal is to give customers in highly regulated environments the ability to: (1) restrict egress to a minimal, auditable set of endpoints per-component; (2) perform staged upgrades when full internet egress is either undesirable or impossible; and (3) recover/rollback safely when network constraints or partial failures occur.

Motivation:
Current private deploy upgrade paths assume either full egress or a fully air-gapped operator-assisted workflow. Customers have requested a middle ground: a decomposed egress model where control-plane components can reach a small, allowlisted set of Redwood services (manifest signing, image index, attestation), while data-plane workloads remain isolated. Additionally, we need deterministic upgrade acceptance criteria when mirror syncs or partial-proxy tunnels are used for artifact distribution.

Goals (must have):
- Define a per-component egress allowlist and an acceptance contract for staged image/manifest distribution under limited bandwidth windows.
- Provide an operator-less verification mode that validates image provenance using signed manifests and local checksum reconciliation (supports airgap and limited-egress customers).
- Define rollback/contingency criteria and automated safe-fail behavior for upgrades that encounter network partitioning or mirror lag.

Non-goals (out of scope):
- Full implementation of physical-media (USB) artifact transfer. See PM-13502 for that track.
- Redesign of the entire operator lifecycle; this is additive and must be compatible with existing operator flows.

Assumptions:
- Customers can provision an internal mirror host or an allowlistable proxy endpoint in their VPC for artifact caching.
- KMS/HSM integrations are already available for signing keys; this PRD assumes Redwood can deliver signed manifests accessible via minimal egress.
- Network ACLs and egress controls are enforced by customer infra; Redwood must provide clear endpoint and port lists.

Requirements (functional):
1) Egress Decomposition and Allowlists:
  - Provide a canonical per-component manifest that lists minimal endpoints + ports required for bootstrap, manifest fetch, attestation, and telemetry (optional).
  - Support two egress profiles: MINIMAL (control-plane only: manifest index, signature verification, attestation) and MIRROR (control-plane + mirror host for images).
  - Document behavior when components cannot reach an endpoint in either profile (fail-fast for non-critical telemetry; staged-retry for manifests).
2) Signed-Manifests and Operator-less Verification:
  - All release artifacts (images, operator charts, control-plane manifests) must have SHA256 checksums and be referenced by a signed top-level manifest.
  - Provide a local verification CLI (or operator subcommand) that validates signatures against a pinned public key and verifies checksums before applying images.
3) Staged Mirror Sync and Bandwidth-Aware Upgrade Window:
  - Define a staged sync protocol: manifest -> shard-level index -> artifact pull. Support resumable downloads and rate-limiting per-host to respect customer bandwidth windows.
  - Allow customers to specify a maintenance window and expected mirror sync throughput; the system must estimate completion time and refuse canary start if sync < canary threshold.
4) Rollback and Safe-Fail Behavior:
  - If a node detects missing artifacts or failed checksum verification, it must roll back to the previous pinned version and emit a deterministic incident event and traceback to the console (telemetry optional under MINIMAL egress).
  - Provide an automated fallback path: if mirror sync fails repeatedly, operator can switch to a pre-authorized local-image-store mode where images are consumed from a specified on-host path.
5) Observability and Audit Trails:
  - Every manifest fetch, signature verification, artifact checksum validation, and stage transition must be recorded in an audit log with timestamps and component-level identifiers. Logs must be exportable as ndjson for SIEM ingestion.
  - Upgrade progress dashboard: percent-of-artifacts-synced, per-host lag, estimated completion, and a health state for each rollout stage.
6) Compatibility and Interop:
  - Backwards compatible with existing private-deploy operator versions (>= operator-1.9). Provide migration notes and a compatibility matrix.

Non-functional requirements:
- Performance: manifest verification time per node should be <= 2s for typical manifest sizes (< 256KB).
- Security: use RSA-4096 or ECDSA-P384 for manifest signatures; keys are rotated per customer policy.
- Resilience: mirror sync protocol must support resumption after interruptions and detect partial-file corruption and retry from the last verified chunk.

Acceptance Criteria:
(See separate acceptance_criteria array for machine-readable checks).

Operational Playbook (high level):
- Operator runbook steps for a limited-egress upgrade: 1) validate mirror host accessibility; 2) run local verification against signed manifest; 3) start staged sync with capacity estimate; 4) perform canary on single dedicated node with NO telemetry flag; 5) validate correctness via checksum+smoke tests; 6) proceed with rolling upgrade or rollback on failure.

Risks & Mitigations:
- Risk: Customers misconfigure allowlists and block required endpoints. Mitigation: Provide a preflight check tool that simulates minimal egress and reports missing endpoints and ports.
- Risk: Mirror lag causing partial upgrades and split-brain versions. Mitigation: Enforce canary-success threshold and binary gating: if mirror sync percentage < 95% do not continue.

acceptance_criteria: Signed-manifest validation: for any release, a local verification run must confirm the top-level manifest signature and verify checksums for all referenced artifacts before any image is applied.

Egress profiles published: MINIMAL and MIRROR endpoint lists (hostnames/IPs + ports) published in plain-text and machine-readable formats; preflight tool succeeds with network conditions matching published lists.
Mirror sync gating: staged sync progress must reach >=95% of artifacts within the configured maintenance window for canary stage to start; otherwise rollout is blocked.
Resumable downloads: interrupted artifact downloads must resume and complete without restarting from zero; verified via integration test that simulates mid-transfer interruption.
Rollback determinism: a node that fails verification must automatically rollback to previous pinned version and emit an audit event with reason and checksum mismatch detail.
On-host fallback: documented and tested procedure to switch to on-host image-store mode and complete upgrade from local artifacts without external egress.
Audit logs: all manifest and artifact events are recorded and exportable as ndjson; sample export validated in QA with at least one upgrade run.
Console visibility: upgrade dashboard displays per-host sync percentage, estimated completion, and a clear 'blocked-by-network' state when gating applies.
Preflight tool: network preflight returns PASS/FAIL and enumerates missing endpoints; must be bundled with release and validated against three customer network topologies in staging.
Compatibility: upgrade flow tested against operator-1.9 and operator-1.10 clusters; migration notes included in PRD and release notes.
